## Files and setup

1. Download [`weather_stations.db`](https://github.com/thomasnield/oreilly_getting_started_with_sql/blob/master/weather_stations.db) from the [course-material repository](https://github.com/thomasnield/oreilly_getting_started_with_sql).
2. Open the database in DB Browser for SQLite, SQLiteStudio, or another SQLite client approved by your instructor.
3. Locate the `STATION_DATA` table.
4. Write and execute one query for every question.
5. Paste each query into the corresponding SQL block in this document. When requested, record the result below the query.

::: {.callout-note title="Protect the source data"}
This is a read-only assignment. Do not use `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `DROP`, or `ALTER`.
:::

## Database reference

The assignment uses the `STATION_DATA` table.

| Column | Stored data |
|---|---|
| `station_number` | Weather-station identifier |
| `report_code` | Report identifier or code |
| `year`, `month`, `day` | Observation date components |
| `dew_point` | Dew-point measurement |
| `station_pressure` | Station-pressure measurement |
| `visibility` | Visibility measurement |
| `wind_speed` | Wind-speed measurement |
| `temperature` | Temperature measurement |
| `precipitation` | Precipitation measurement |
| `snow_depth` | Snow-depth measurement |
| `fog`, `rain`, `hail`, `thunder`, `tornado` | Weather indicators stored as `1` for true and `0` for false |

Use the measurement values in the units in which they are stored in the database. You do not need to convert units.


## Part A


1. Select every column and the first 10 rows from `STATION_DATA`.


2. Select only `station_number`, `year`, `month`, `day`, and `temperature` from `STATION_DATA`.


3. Select `station_number`, `report_code`, `precipitation`, `rain`, and `thunder`. Rename `precipitation` as `precip_amount` in the query output.

## Part B


1. Return `station_number`, `year`, `month`, `day`, and `temperature` for observations recorded in the year 2000.


2. Return the date columns, `station_number`, and `precipitation` for observations from 2000 through 2009, inclusive, that recorded precipitation greater than zero.

3. Return `station_number`, the date columns, `dew_point`, and `station_pressure` for records in which both `dew_point` and `station_pressure` are not missing. Limit the query to observations from June, July, or August.

## Part C

1. Return `station_number`, the date columns, and `precipitation`. Sort the results from the greatest precipitation to the least precipitation and display only the first 20 rows.

2. Return `station_number`, the date columns, and `temperature`. Sort first by `station_number` in ascending order and then by date from newest to oldest.

## Part D

1. Count the number of observations in each year. Name the count `observation_count` and return one row per year.
2. For each calendar month, calculate the average, minimum, and maximum temperature. Use clear aliases for all three calculated columns.

3. For each `station_number`, count the number of records that have precipitation greater than zero. Name the count `precipitation_report_count`.

## Part E

1. Group the data by year and count the number of records in which `tornado = 1`. Keep only years with at least one tornado record. Sort the year with the greatest count first.

2. Count the number of observations for each `station_number`. Keep only stations with at least 100 observations and sort from the largest count to the smallest count.

3. For each year and month, calculate the average wind speed and count the nonmissing wind-speed values. Keep only groups that have at least 20 nonmissing wind-speed values. Sort the results by year and then month, both in ascending order.

## Part F

1. Write one query that uses `SELECT`, `WHERE`, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, and `ORDER BY`.

Your query must:

- use only records from 2000 through 2009, inclusive;
- exclude records with missing precipitation;
- group the remaining records by year and month;
- calculate total precipitation and name it `total_precipitation`;
- keep only year-month groups whose total precipitation is greater than 5; and
- sort from the greatest total precipitation to the least.
